chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the one in Ihram wearing Khazz (animal fur). He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem'.

key_terms.الْخَزَّ: Khazz, a type of fabric often identified as animal fur or silk, worn by the Muhrim
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a pilgrim in Ihram to wear animal fur (Khazz)?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that Khazz, often identified as fine silk or a specific type of fur, is permissible for the Muhrim to wear, distinguishing it from the strictly prohibited woven silk (Dibaj). This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between different types of luxurious fabrics, emphasizing that not all fine textiles are forbidden during the sacred state of Ihram, thereby offering practical guidance for pilgrims seeking to balance comfort with ritual purity.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj who said,
‘I asked Abu Al-Hassanasws about the one in Ihraam wearing Al-Khazz (animal fur). Heasws said: ‘There is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 12. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali from Ahmad ibn ‘A’idh from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, if one in the state of Ihram can wear black cloths. He (the Imam) said, ‘One cannot assume the state of Ihram in black cloths or use it for shrouding therewith . ‘“
